youtube.baslik: Noise Exposure Limits: 80, 85 and 87 dB(A) | Lesson 222 | AIHEAR Audiology Academy
youtube.aciklama:
At what level does workplace noise require action? In this lesson we compare the action and limit values of European Union Directive 2003/10/EC and the 2013 noise regulation in Türkiye, the peak values (135, 137 and 140 dB(C)), weekly exposure, the difference between the 3 dB and 5 dB exchange rates, and the NIOSH and OSHA criteria.

AIHEAR Audiology Academy makes short, clear lessons for audiology students and professionals.

Sources: European Parliament and Council, Directive 2003/10/EC on noise; Regulation on the Protection of Employees from Noise-Related Risks, Türkiye, Official Gazette 28.07.2013, No. 28721; NIOSH, Criteria for a Recommended Standard: Occupational Noise Exposure (1998); OSHA, 29 CFR 1910.95; ISO 1999, Acoustics: Estimation of noise-induced hearing loss.

This video is for educational purposes and does not replace diagnosis or treatment.

sahneler.alt: Action values, peak values and exchange rate
cumleler: Hello, and welcome to the AIHEAR Audiology Academy.
In this lesson we will learn the action and limit values that set the noise levels at which action is required at work.
We will also compare peak values, weekly exposure and the difference between the 3 decibel and 5 decibel exchange rates.

maddeler.metin: Sets the action level in numbers

cumleler: Limit values set in numbers when noise at a workplace requires action.
These values are based on studies of hearing loss risk in workers exposed to noise over many years.

cumleler.yazi: The international standard ISO 1999 offers a method to predict expected hearing loss from the level and duration of exposure.
cumleler.ses: The international standard ISO nineteen ninety nine offers a method to predict expected hearing loss from the level and duration of exposure.

cumleler: No limit value reduces risk to zero; it only brings it down to an acceptable level.
So staying below the limit does not make protective measures unnecessary.
In this lesson we first compare the European and Türkiye values, then two different approaches in the United States.

notlar.metin: EU directive and Türkiye: same values

cumleler.yazi: The 2003 noise directive of the European Union and the 2013 regulation in Türkiye use the same three values.
cumleler.ses: The two thousand three noise directive of the European Union and the twenty thirteen regulation in Türkiye use the same three values.

cumleler: The values are expressed as the daily noise exposure level, the average level normalized to an eight-hour working day.

cumleler.yazi: The lower exposure action value is 80 dB(A).
cumleler.ses: The lower exposure action value is eighty decibels A.

cumleler.yazi: The upper exposure action value is 85 dB(A).
cumleler.ses: The upper exposure action value is eighty five decibels A.

cumleler.yazi: The exposure limit value is 87 dB(A), and it must not be exceeded.
cumleler.ses: The exposure limit value is eighty seven decibels A, and it must not be exceeded.

cumleler: In the regulation, these are named the lower exposure action value, the upper exposure action value and the exposure limit value.
The limit value has one important difference: it is assessed taking into account the protection given by the hearing protector.
Each threshold places different duties on the employer.

cumleler.yazi: Above 80 dB(A), hearing protectors are made available and workers receive information and training.
cumleler.ses: Above eighty decibels A, hearing protectors are made available and workers receive information and training.

cumleler: At this level, hearing tests may also be provided if the risk assessment shows a health risk.

cumleler.yazi: At 85 dB(A) and above, the use of hearing protectors is ensured and enforced.
cumleler.ses: At eighty five decibels A and above, the use of hearing protectors is ensured and enforced.

cumleler: At this level, work areas are marked, measures to reduce noise are put in place and the employer arranges hearing tests.

cumleler.yazi: And 87 dB(A) is the upper limit that exposure at the ear must not exceed, even with protectors worn.
cumleler.ses: And eighty seven decibels A is the upper limit that exposure at the ear must not exceed, even with protectors worn.

cumleler: If this limit is exceeded, the employer acts at once, identifies the cause and makes changes to prevent it happening again.
Let us look at an example of how the limit value is assessed together with the protector.

cumleler.yazi: Suppose a worker's daily exposure level is 95 dB(A).
cumleler.ses: Suppose a worker's daily exposure level is ninety five decibels A.

cumleler: Assume the protector gives this worker about 12 decibels of attenuation in real use.

cumleler.yazi: The effective level at the ear is then about 83 dB(A), which stays below the 87 dB(A) limit value.
cumleler.ses: The effective level at the ear is then about eighty three decibels A, which stays below the eighty seven decibels A limit value.

cumleler.yazi: However, action values are assessed without the protector, so the 85 dB(A) duties still apply to this worker.
cumleler.ses: However, action values are assessed without the protector, so the eighty five decibels A duties still apply to this worker.

cumleler: In other words, wearing protectors is mandatory, hearing tests are done and noise reduction work continues.
For impulse noise, the average level is not enough; the very brief peak sound pressure is also limited separately.
Peak values are measured with C weighting, because C weighting suppresses low frequencies much less than A weighting.

cumleler.yazi: The peak limit is 135 dB(C) for the lower action value and 137 dB(C) for the upper action value.
cumleler.ses: The peak limit is one hundred thirty five decibels C for the lower action value and one hundred thirty seven decibels C for the upper action value.

cumleler.yazi: The peak limit for the exposure limit value is 140 dB(C).
cumleler.ses: The peak limit for the exposure limit value is one hundred forty decibels C.

cumleler: In work such as presses, riveting, blasting and shooting, peak values can come close to these limits.
Peak values matter in their own right, because even a single very loud impulse can cause acoustic trauma.

maddeler.metin: When exposure varies day to day
Weekly exposure level can be used

cumleler: In some jobs, noise exposure varies markedly from one day to the next.
In this case, the regulation allows the weekly noise exposure level to be used instead of the daily level.
The weekly level is an average based on a working week of five days with eight hours a day.

cumleler.yazi: However, the weekly level also cannot exceed the 87 dB(A) limit value, and measures to reduce risk are taken.
cumleler.ses: However, the weekly level also cannot exceed the eighty seven decibels A limit value, and measures to reduce risk are taken.

cumleler: In this way, the load of a busy day is balanced by the other days of the week, but the limit is kept.
If the weekly level is used, measurements must be planned so that they represent the whole week.
The exchange rate shows by how many decibels the level must rise for the allowed time to be cut in half.

cumleler.yazi: Europe, Türkiye, ISO 1999 and NIOSH, the US occupational health research institute, use a 3 decibel exchange rate.
cumleler.ses: Europe, Türkiye, ISO nineteen ninety nine and NIOSH, the US occupational health research institute, use a three decibel exchange rate.

cumleler: This rate is based on the equal energy principle: when sound rises by 3 decibels, its energy doubles.

cumleler.yazi: On the blue curve, 85 dB(A) allows 8 hours, 88 allows 4 hours, 91 allows 2 hours and 94 allows 1 hour.
cumleler.ses: On the blue curve, eighty five decibels A allows eight hours, eighty eight allows four hours, ninety one allows two hours and ninety four allows one hour.

cumleler.yazi: OSHA, the US regulatory agency, uses a 5 decibel exchange rate and a permissible limit of 90 dB(A).
cumleler.ses: OSHA, the US regulatory agency, uses a five decibel exchange rate and a permissible limit of ninety decibels A.

cumleler.yazi: On the dashed line, 90 dB(A) allows 8 hours, 95 allows 4 hours and 100 allows 2 hours.
cumleler.ses: On the dashed line, ninety decibels A allows eight hours, ninety five allows four hours and one hundred allows two hours.

cumleler.yazi: For example, at 100 dB(A) the 3 decibel rule allows only 15 minutes, while the 5 decibel rule allows 2 hours.
cumleler.ses: For example, at one hundred decibels A the three decibel rule allows only fifteen minutes, while the five decibel rule allows two hours.

cumleler: The 5 decibel rule assumes that the ear partly recovers during quiet breaks in the working day.
However, this assumption does not hold in every workplace, and the scientific evidence mostly supports the equal energy principle.

cumleler.yazi: In its 1998 criteria document, NIOSH adopted a recommended limit of 85 dB(A) and a 3 decibel exchange rate.
cumleler.ses: In its nineteen ninety eight criteria document, NIOSH adopted a recommended limit of eighty five decibels A and a three decibel exchange rate.

cumleler.yazi: According to NIOSH, even workers exposed to 85 dB(A) over a 40-year working life have an excess risk of hearing loss of about 8 percent.
cumleler.ses: According to NIOSH, even workers exposed to eighty five decibels A over a forty year working life have an excess risk of hearing loss of about eight percent.

cumleler.yazi: According to the same document, this risk rises to about 25 percent at 90 dB(A).
cumleler.ses: According to the same document, this risk rises to about twenty five percent at ninety decibels A.

cumleler: These numbers clearly show that staying below the limit value does not remove the risk.
This table shows the main regulations side by side.

cumleler.yazi: Europe and Türkiye use thresholds of 80, 85 and 87 dB(A) and a 3 decibel exchange rate.
cumleler.ses: Europe and Türkiye use thresholds of eighty, eighty five and eighty seven decibels A and a three decibel exchange rate.

cumleler.yazi: NIOSH recommends 85 dB(A) and 3 decibels; this is a scientific recommendation, not a law.
cumleler.ses: NIOSH recommends eighty five decibels A and three decibels; this is a scientific recommendation, not a law.

cumleler.yazi: Under OSHA, 85 dB(A) is the action level that starts a hearing conservation program, and 90 dB(A) is the legal limit.
cumleler.ses: Under OSHA, eighty five decibels A is the action level that starts a hearing conservation program, and ninety decibels A is the legal limit.

cumleler: For impulse noise, all three sources use a peak value of 140 decibels as the upper limit.
Let us summarize in a flow how the values are used at work.
First, noise is measured, and the daily exposure level and peak value are found for each worker.
The results are compared with the action and limit values.
Depending on which threshold is exceeded, protectors, signs, training and noise reduction measures are applied.
Finally, audiometric monitoring is carried out, and measurements are repeated as the work environment changes.
We will cover measurement methods and dosimetry in detail in the next lesson.
Limit values are designed for exposure at work; noise in daily life also adds to the total risk.
Concerts, personal music players and hobby tools are important sources of noise outside work.
Some people are more susceptible to noise than others; the same exposure can cause different degrees of loss.
That is why audiometric monitoring and training are valuable even below the action values.
If monitoring shows a meaningful threshold change, measures are reviewed even when exposure is below the limits.
We will cover safe listening advice in the lesson on recreational noise.

sahneler.metin: When assessing the limit value, do not trust the protector's packaging value; attenuation in real use is often lower.

cumleler.yazi: A clinical tip: when assessing the 87 dB(A) limit value, do not rely on the value printed on the protector's packaging.
cumleler.ses: A clinical tip: when assessing the eighty seven decibels A limit value, do not rely on the value printed on the protector's packaging.

cumleler: In real use, the attenuation that protectors give is often lower than the label states.
If possible, carry out an individual fit test for the worker, or use a realistic correction.
We will cover protector selection and fit testing in detail in a later lesson.

cumleler.yazi: In Türkiye and Europe, the action values are 80 and 85, and the exposure limit value is 87 dB(A).
cumleler.ses: In Türkiye and Europe, the action values are eighty and eighty five, and the exposure limit value is eighty seven decibels A.

cumleler.yazi: For impulse noise, the peak values are 135, 137 and 140 dB(C).
cumleler.ses: For impulse noise, the peak values are one hundred thirty five, one hundred thirty seven and one hundred forty decibels C.

cumleler: The limit value is assessed taking into account the protection given by the hearing protector.
The 3 decibel rule, based on the equal energy principle, is more protective than the 5 decibel rule of OSHA.

sahneler.aciklama: 87 dB(A) is assessed _with the protector_ counted.

The correct answer is C: 87 dB(A).
cumleler.ses: The correct answer is C: eighty seven decibels A.

cumleler.yazi: 80 and 85 dB(A) are action values; 87 dB(A) is the limit that must not be exceeded even with protectors worn.
cumleler.ses: Eighty and eighty five decibels A are action values; eighty seven decibels A is the limit that must not be exceeded even with protectors worn.
